description: Dark matter external validation against independent databases
conclusion: External validation with IntAct (105,122 yeast interactions) confirms that 0/44 dark matter pairs are recorded in any independent PPI database. These are genuinely hidden functional associations: 83.1% of the dark matter proteins are individually known to IntAct, but their pairwise functional relationships have never been experimentally observed. The embedding geometry predicts functional associations that remain invisible to all existing experimental PPI detection methods. FDR-corrected GO enrichment identifies 1/4 tested terms as significant (FDR < 0.05).

deep_analysis.interpretation: 0/44 dark matter pairs are recorded in IntAct, confirming they are genuinely hidden functional associations invisible to all PPI databases tested (STRING + IntAct). However, 59/71 dark matter proteins individually appear in IntAct - these are not unknown proteins, but their pairwise functional associations have never been experimentally observed. This is the defining characteristic of functional dark matter: known proteins with known functions, but unknown pairwise functional relationships.
deep_analysis.dm_protein_coverage: 59/71 (83.1%) of dark matter proteins are individually annotated in IntAct
